mlp.memoryMethod: trainMemoryMeasuredMB = peak process RSS minus RSS before the training loop (psutil; includes framework/allocator noise). trainMemoryAnalyticMB = analytical estimate: params x 4 B x (weights + grad + 2 Adam states) + 2 x batch(256) x activations(140) x 4 B.

elm.note: trainELM standardizes the targets internally (yMean/yStd stored in the model); elmPredict de-standardizes.
elm.memoryMethod: trainMemoryAnalyticMB = bytes of A (hidden^2) + B (hidden x 3) + W + b + beta as Float64. trainMemoryMeasuredMB = process.memoryUsage().rss after trainELM minus rss before (after global.gc(), run with node --expose-gc); an RSS delta, not a peak, and noisy at this size.

baseline.description: Predicts each target as the TRAIN mean within the same (sequenceId, irrigation, texture, slopeClass, sowOffsetDays) group, ignoring climate; falls back to the global train mean when a group is empty.

speedupNote: speedupVsSimulator compares the model forward pass against the simulator core (runSequence, 24 years averaged per year) with features and ET0 already precomputed.
split: test = year 2019-2024 OR pointId heldOut (asuncionmita, gualan, rabinal, sanarate); train = rest
caveat: The spatial hold-out is not fully independent: NASA POWER cells are 0.5 degrees, so some held-out points fall in the same cell as a training point (identical elevation and tmax series). Held-out points sharing a POWER cell with a training point: gualan (with chiquimula, jocotan, zacapa); sanarate (with guastatoya); asuncionmita (with jutiapa, santacatarinamita, jalapa, monjas, cuilapa); rabinal (with sanmartin, salama, cubulco). Rainfall (IMERG/ERA5) and some other climate features may still differ, but temperature and radiation are shared. Use bySplit.testYears (temporal hold-out at non-held-out points) as the cleanest generalization estimate; testPoints and testBoth mix both effects.
